legacyDisplayName: TC-ROLE-001: A Branch Manager sees Harrow operational data and is rejected for another branch
TC-ROLE-001b: A Branch Manager cannot create or archive a branch (lifecycle is super-admin only)
TC-ROLE-002: A Deputy Manager CAN view Harrow enquiries, update status, and add notes
TC-ROLE-002b: A Deputy Manager CANNOT view org-wide user/account management
TC-ROLE-002c: A Deputy Manager CANNOT access another branch's enquiries
TC-ROLE-002d-REG (regression, CRITICAL): A Deputy Manager CANNOT grant themselves or anyone else super_admin
TC-ROLE-002e-REG (regression): the SAME escalation attempt via UPDATE (upgrading an existing login) is also rejected
TC-ROLE-002f: super_admin itself CAN still grant super_admin (the fix blocks escalation, not legitimate admin work)
TC-ROLE-003: an already-issued access token keeps its OLD role's permissions until it's refreshed (documented session policy)
TC-ROLE-003b: logging back in AFTER the downgrade correctly reflects the NEW, reduced permissions
TC-STAFFATT-002-REG (regression): clock-out with NO prior clock-in that day is rejected
TC-STAFFATT-001: Clock-in records status Present, a clock_in timestamp, and clears any missing-clockout flag
TC-STAFFATT-001-REG (regression): a duplicate clock-in the same day is rejected, not silently overwritten
TC-STAFFATT-002: Clock-out closes the session and computes worked minutes
TC-STAFFATT-002b-REG (regression): a second clock-out the same day is rejected
TC-STAFFATT-003: A manual correction backfills a day the kiosk never captured (create-on-correct), audited with a reason
TC-STAFFATT-003b: A manual correction on an EXISTING record updates status and appends to its correction history
TC-STAFFATT-004: Marking a clocked-in staff member Absent clears their clock-in/out times
TC-STAFFATT-004b: The attendance-summary KPI payload is well-formed for a scoped branch/date
TC-STAFFATT-004c: Clocking in an unknown staff id is rejected, not a 500
TC-STAFFATT-003c: A clock-in left open on a PAST date is flagged in the missing-clockout KPI immediately, with no hours calculated for the open shift
TC-CHILDATT-004-REG (regression, safeguarding): check-out with NO prior check-in that day is rejected
TC-CHILDATT-001: Check-in records status Present, timestamp, and the checking-in staff member
TC-CHILDATT-001-REG (regression): a duplicate check-in the same day is rejected, not silently overwritten
TC-CHILDATT-002: Check-out closes the session and records the timestamp
TC-CHILDATT-002-REG (regression): a second check-out the same day is rejected
TC-CHILDATT-004b: re-checking in after a check-out (same day, e.g. re-entry) is allowed and clears the stale check-out
TC-CHILDATT-004c: check-in for a nonexistent child is rejected, not a 500
TC-CHILDATT-003 (regression, documents a real gap): checking in a child on a day with no scheduled session succeeds silently, with no 'unscheduled' flag
TC-SCHEDULE-001: A Mon/Wed/Fri full-day schedule persists and is reflected in the room's capacity forecast, not Tue/Thu
TC-SCHEDULE-002: Changing Friday to Thursday updates the schedule — Friday occupancy decreases, Thursday increases
TC-CHILDROOM-001: Existing Harrow rooms carry sane, non-overlapping age ranges for the recommendation logic
TC-CHILDROOM-004-REG (regression, Critical/safeguarding): a room-only update does NOT wipe allergies or medical notes
Exit Criteria §6 (regression): a second child with the same name and date of birth at the same branch is rejected, not silently duplicated
SEC-001: No token is rejected with 401, not data or a 500
SEC-002: A malformed bearer token is rejected with 401, not a 500
SEC-003 (regression): NoSQL operator injection via query-string values stays a literal, inert string
SEC-004 (regression): a malformed regex in the staff search box no longer causes a raw 500
SEC-004b (regression): same malformed-regex fix on the children search endpoint
SEC-004c (regression): same malformed-regex fix on the daily-records search endpoint
SEC-005: A regex-escaped search still finds real matches (the fix didn't break normal substring search)
SEC-006 (regression): JSON body type confusion (object where a string field is expected) is rejected, not silently coerced
SEC-007: An explicit branch filter never returns another branch's records
TC-AUTH-003 (regression): repeated failed logins from one caller are rate-limited
note: Verified individually in isolation (12/12 sequential attempts producing the expected 401/429 mix). Deliberately NOT run as part of routine collection runs except a final, deliberate full-collection pass, since it burns the shared per-IP login rate-limit budget (middleware.RateLimit(10, time.Minute), shared by /auth/login and /admin/auth/login) that every other suite's Setup depends on. Must stay the LAST case in SUI-AUTH-001, which must stay the LAST suite in COL-FUNC-001.

legacyDisplayName: TC-ENQ-001 (adapted, admin-logged channel): a new enquiry is created exactly once, status New, linked to Harrow
TC-ENQ-004: The enquiry is visible under Harrow with complete parent/child information
TC-ENQ-005: An internal note is added, author and timestamp are recorded
TC-ENQ-006: Status New -> Contacted is a single, auditable transition
TC-VISIT-001 (expressed as a status transition): Contacted -> Booked visit
TC-VISIT-004 (expressed as a status transition): Booked visit -> Visit completed
TC-REG-001: Registering the enquiry creates exactly one Child, links the enquiry, sets status Registered
TC-REG-001b (regression): the expected start date round-trips to the exact same calendar date, no timezone shift
TC-REG-002: The enquiry appears exactly once under Registered, and nowhere else
TC-REG-003: Registering the same enquiry a second time does not create a second child
TC-ENQ-002: A name is required to create an enquiry
TC-ENQ-002b: Either an email or a phone number is required
TC-ENQ-002c: A branch is required
TC-ENQ-002d: An enquiry type is required
TC-ENQ-003 (regression): submitting the same enquiry twice merges into one record instead of creating a duplicate
TC-ENQ-003b: A submission from the same email AFTER the first is Registered is treated as a genuinely new enquiry, not merged
TC-REG-004 (regression, documents a real gap): registering with no child fields still flips the enquiry to Registered — no atomicity ties status to child creation
TC-ROOM-001 (adapted): Harrow's existing (non-test-debris) rooms have valid capacity
TC-ROOM-001b: Creating a new room with valid data succeeds exactly once
TC-ROOM-002 (regression): capacity of zero is rejected
TC-ROOM-002 (regression): negative capacity is rejected
TC-ROOM-002 (regression): duplicate room name within the same branch is rejected
TC-ROOM-002b: the same room name is allowed in a DIFFERENT branch
TC-ROOM-002c: missing room name is rejected
TC-AUTH-001: Director/admin login succeeds and returns a usable session
TC-AUTH-001b: The returned access token is immediately usable
TC-AUTH-002: Invalid password is rejected with a safe, generic message
TC-AUTH-002b: Login for a non-existent email returns the SAME error shape as a wrong password
TC-BR-001 (adapted): Harrow branch exists exactly once, active, with a unique slug
TC-BR-001b: Branch KPIs are non-negative and internally consistent (occupancy <= 100%)
TC-BR-002: Creating a second branch with slug=harrow is rejected, no partial record created
TC-BR-002b: Double-submitting the exact same duplicate-slug request twice both fail cleanly
TC-BR-003: Address, opening hours, and capacity are configurable and round-trip via PUT
TC-BR-003b (regression, documents a real gap): an invalid opening-hours entry is accepted, not rejected
TC-STAFF-001: A new staff member is created exactly once, linked to Harrow, status active
TC-STAFF-001b: An invalid status value is rejected
TC-STAFF-003 (regression): duplicate email on create is rejected
TC-STAFF-003b (regression): duplicate email on UPDATE (renaming someone else onto an existing email) is rejected
TC-STAFF-003c: Updating a staff member's OWN email to its own current value is allowed (not a false-positive duplicate)
TC-STAFF-004-REG (regression, Critical/data-loss): a room-only update does NOT wipe email, phone, or job title
TC-LOG-001: A meal log is created with meal_type/eaten, a minted ref, and the type's default status
TC-LOG-001b (validation): a record with no title is rejected
TC-LOG-001c (validation): a record with no branch_slug is rejected
TC-LOG-001d (regression): an unknown field in the request body is rejected, not silently ignored
TC-LOG-004: An activity/observation log persists its EYFS areas and next steps
TC-LOG-004b: An observation's status can be moved through its real lifecycle (logged -> resolved)
TC-LOG-005: An incident/accident record defaults to status Open and keeps its severity
TC-LOG-005b (regression, safeguarding): deleting an incident is a real, non-recoverable delete — but is captured in the audit log
TC-LOG-006: The daily summary aggregation is well-formed and includes a by_type breakdown
TC-LOG-006b: Fetching a nonexistent daily record is rejected with 404, not a 500
Exit Criteria §6 (regression): a rapid double-submit of the identical log entry merges into one record, but a genuinely different entry the same day does not
